subject: Metering and baseline pricing: Chat vs Responses vs legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@neoretail.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T12:22:00-04:00
Subject: Quick question on billing units across endpoints

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo today — feels like Redwood could help us reduce latency and token costs on our search + assistant flows. Before we share anything with procurement, a couple of quick clarifying questions on the hosted pricing:

1) For Chat Completions vs the newer Responses endpoint, are tokens billed the same way? Our engineering team is trying to reconcile token counts coming out of the Responses call vs what we see in the chat endpoint on the POC.

2) Is the legacy /v1/completions endpoint still billed under the same unit as Responses, or is that a separate SKU? We have some older microservices still calling the legacy endpoint and procurement wants to map SKUs to their internal chargeback.

3) If we sign up for a baseline committed monthly spend (reserved capacity), does that apply uniformly across endpoints, or are there per-endpoint multipliers?

If possible can you send a short example mapping or example invoice line-items we can show finance?

Appreciate it — Sam

—
Sam Carter
Head of Platform
NeoRetail
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@neoretail.io>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@neoretail.io>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on billing units across endpoints

Hi Sam,

Great question — thanks for sending these. Short answer: units are conceptually aligned but there are important distinctions you should show procurement. I'll put the high-level mapping below and attach a simple spreadsheet mapping line-items. If that looks good we can slot in 30 minutes with finance/engineering to walk your team through an example invoice.

High-level:
- Responses API: metered per-response token (input + output) with a single hosted SKU.
- Chat Completions: billed per-turn tokens (input + output) but historically mapped to a chat-specific SKU; in our hosted ratecard we show equivalent token-normalized price so finance can reconcile.
- Legacy /v1/completions: still charged but often appears as a different invoice line (legacy-completions SKU) — we recommend migrating to Responses for clearer unit parity.

I'll follow up internally for the more detailed per-token examples and reserve capacity implications. Attaching a mapping sheet and a draft SOW the procurement team can review.

Thanks — Grace

Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick question on billing units across endpoints

Forwarding Sam's note — NeoRetail wants a concise mapping they can push to procurement (example invoice lines + recommendation). Can you help with an engineer-friendly note on how Responses token accounting maps to chat-turn accounting and any gotchas (prompt truncation, system messages, function-calls)? Also: we should propose a baseline commit suggestion (monthly $) and a discount band. Sam indicated they run ~45M tokens/month today across various services.

Key ask:
- One-page mapping: Responses token model -> Chat turn model -> legacy completions SKU
- Recommended baseline (commit) for 45M tokens and suggested discount tiers & renewal cadence

Thanks — Grace
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on billing units across endpoints

Grace — below is a compact technical mapping you can share with NeoRetail. Kept it short for procurement.

Responses API (current):
- Metering: input tokens + output tokens per response call.
- Example: single Responses call with 2,000 input tokens and 500 output tokens => 2,500 billable tokens.

Chat Completions (chat-turn model):
- Metering: each turn includes role tokens (system + user + assistant). Historically chunked into chat SKU where multi-turn contexts can leverage prefix/KV caching; invoice shows chat-turn lines but we can normalize to token-equivalent price.
- Example: 3-turn exchange where first prompt = 600 tokens, second turn adds 300 input tokens, output tokens sum to 800 => billable ~1,700 tokens (subject to session caching savings if repeated prefixes).

Legacy /v1/completions:
- Metering: older SKU; billed per completion tokens but often lacks the modern normalization to Responses. For migration we recommend switching to Responses and mapping 1:1 on token counts; we handle quota/fallback compatibility.

Commit handling:
- Baseline commit applies at the account level across hosted endpoints. Commit discounts are applied to your monthly bill after token metering. There are no enforced per-endpoint multipliers by default, but enterprise deals may carve out exceptions for dedicated capacity.

Discount guidance for 45M tokens/month (ballpark):
- 0% baseline: standard published per-token rate (hosted).
- 10% commit for a 6-12 month monthly minimum (~$X/month equivalent)
- 18-25% for larger annual commitments or reserved Dedicated pools (depends on GPU mix & SLA).

I attached a one-page CSV (billing-mapping.xlsx) with token examples and a sample invoice line mapping. If procurement wants an actual invoice preview we'll need a hubspot/deal ID — Aditya can confirm discount authority.

-Karthik

--Attachment: billing-mapping.xlsx (token_examples.csv)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

- A 6-month monthly commit at 45M tokens/month at a 12% discount off hosted list, with a mid-term review at month 4 to evaluate uplift.
- Include optional migration credits (one-time $5k credit) if they commit to migrating legacy completions to Responses within 90 days.

Grace: send the proposed SOW + example invoice lines and present the 30-minute review with their finance team. If procurement pushes back, escalate to me before counter-offering deeper discounts.

-Aditya
